source_user: Advanced cluster case GDS-16: Evaluate GPUDirect Storage for checkpoint and dataset I/O in distributed training. Variant 16 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate storage throughput from GPU DMA, validate filesystem and kernel support, measure queue depth and tail latency, compare CPU-staged I/O, and test restart consistency after interruption. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Assume an authorized, isolated benchmark allocation; platform, filesystem, kernel, driver, and storage details are unknown until measured, and production configuration and data remain unchanged. Inventory GPU, storage, PCIe/NVMe and NUMA topology, filesystem/mount and kernel/runtime versions, container permissions, process and I/O affinity, file layout, request size, queue depth, concurrency, cache state, clocks, thermals, and test duration. Separate storage-device throughput, GPU-DMA transfer, and end-to-end training stall time rather than treating one as a proxy for another.

For this tool-use variant, first collect read-only diagnostics and a small synthetic or disposable-data test; record exact commands, exit codes, and path telemetry before any performance claim. Falsifiable hypothesis: after prerequisites and direct-path activation are independently verified, the specified workload for corpus-05391 will improve useful sustained throughput (GB/s) and/or reduce host CPU use or training I/O stall time versus a matched CPU-staged control, without unacceptable tail latency, retries, integrity errors, or restart inconsistency. A null result or fallback-path measurement falsifies the claimed GDS benefit.

Run matched CPU-staged and GDS treatments with identical payloads, placement, request size, queue depth, concurrency, cache condition, warm-up, repetitions, and duration. Report storage and DMA throughput in GB/s, I/O and training-stall latency in ms with p50/p95/p99, queue depth, CPU/GPU utilization, retries, timeouts, integrity errors, and uncertainty. Validate data with checksums or equivalent and test interruption followed by restart and checkpoint consistency.

Failure/rollback: stop and return to the previously working CPU-staged path if the direct path cannot be evidenced, filesystem or kernel prerequisites fail, checksum/restart validation fails, error or timeout rates exceed predeclared limits, tail latency/stall time regresses beyond the agreed threshold, or link, thermal, filesystem, or storage health leaves safe limits. Do not change mounts, drivers, permissions, or production data without explicit authorization. Evidence required before claiming improvement is topology/version inventory, direct-path telemetry, matched baseline data with units and uncertainty, and successful recovery and rollback logs.

Run matched CPU-staged and GDS treatments with identical payloads, placement, request size, queue depth, concurrency, cache condition, warm-up, repetitions, and duration. Report storage and DMA throughput in GB/s, I/O and training-stall latency in ms with p50/p95/p99, queue depth, CPU/GPU utilization, retries, timeouts, integrity errors, and uncertainty. Validate data with checksums or equivalent and test interruption followed by restart and checkpoint consistency.

Failure/rollback: stop and return to the previously working CPU-staged path if the direct path cannot be evidenced, filesystem or kernel prerequisites fail, checksum/restart validation fails, error or timeout rates exceed predeclared limits, tail latency/stall time regresses beyond the agreed threshold, or link, thermal, filesystem, or storage health leaves safe limits. Do not change mounts, drivers, permissions, or production data without explicit authorization. Evidence required before claiming improvement is topology/version inventory, direct-path telemetry, matched baseline data with units and uncertainty, and successful recovery and rollback logs.
